executiveSummary: GM0798 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its 2025 identity, 16,149 residents, eleven neighbourhoods, five BAG woonplaatsen, twenty-five BRT settlement features, thirty scheduled-transit stop areas, zero in-boundary ProRail stations and four A58/N269/N395 road links are coherent. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Hilvarenbeek is a high-sand, brook-valley and canal municipality: Diessen lies on the Reusel, Diessens Broek is deliberate peak storage, Haghorst lies by the Wilhelminakanaal, and the final municipal vision documents both rapid drainage/drought and waterlogging susceptibility. Two regional LIWO candidate points lie inside the full boundary, but no primary candidate does. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset still emits 1.497411 normalized direct inundation stress, 8,441 affected people-equivalent at T+24 and 8,972 at T+72 without selecting either regional point or any hydraulic footprint. Seven nonzero canonical hazard families reuse the identical eleven-neighbourhood order, contradicting mechanism-specific water, high-sand forest and visitor exposure. The canonical remote-fire preset has no direct flame even though current municipal and safety-region evidence makes local nature fire material; Beekse Bergen festival weekends have historically added roughly 60,000–90,000 visitors, far beyond resident-only exposure. Public water, provider, antenna, care, education, road and observation registers improve context but do not establish live function, topology, backup or restoration. NoData, null, no match and out-of-horizon values remain Unknown, never zero, open or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek, PDOK/Kadaster, Rijkswaterstaat, ProRail and OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Coherent 2025 identity, demography, settlement and transport inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS/PDOK 2025; BRT source date 2025-07-01; NWB Light 2026-08-01; ProRail snapshot 2026; OVapi snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31
supports: The generated feature identifies GM0798 Hilvarenbeek in Noord-Brabant and safety region Midden- en West-Brabant, with center [5.150059770347138, 51.47585342896882], 16,149 residents, density 170/km², 24.9% age 65+ and 2,036 one-person households.

Eleven official neighbourhood rows in five districts sum to 16,155 rounded residents, six above the municipality total (+0.037%), 6,925 households and 4,030 rounded residents age 65+. Independent rounded totals are not values to force into exact agreement.

Five BAG woonplaatsen are Biest-Houtakker, Diessen, Esbeek, Haghorst and Hilvarenbeek. Twenty-five BRT settlement polygons comprise six woonkernen, two deelkernen, three gehuchten and fourteen buurtschappen. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; CBS/BRT are CC BY 4.0.

The generated overview MultiPolygon has 79 coordinate positions versus 998 in the 2025 non-generalized boundary. Full geometry is required for brook, canal, forest, road, defence, asset and raster intersections.

Four logical NWB links are A58 to Tilburg, N269 to Tilburg and Reusel-De Mierden, and N395 to Oirschot. Their scenario-unit nominal capacity is valid only for Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply, not utility flow or guaranteed emergency throughput.

No ProRail station point lies inside GM0798. Thirty grouped OVapi scheduled stop areas do, including Safaripark and Speelland; schedules are best-effort context and do not prove vehicles, drivers, capacity, accessibility or operation during an incident.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Final Omgevingsvisie ‘Samen gezond groeien’
evidenceSources.edition: Final text processed 20 October 2025 following council adoption on 25 September 2025; long-term policy horizon 2050
supports: The adopted spatial-policy evidence class says Hilvarenbeek becomes drier on average, wetter under peak loading and warmer; it is not a current observation or event probability.

Deep drainage dries forest; permeable podzol/dekzand ridges retain water poorly; smaller watercourses drain quickly; and brook valleys both fill in wet periods and experience drying. Reduced storage makes the municipality more vulnerable to waterlogging.

Diessen lies on the Reusel, Haghorst developed beside the Wilhelminakanaal, and the municipal Natura 2000 context includes Roovertsche Heide, Landgoed de Utrecht and the Reusel; Gorp en Roovert and Annanina’s Rust are additional nature-network areas.

The policy seeks water-retention on high sand, space for peak water in brook valleys, future-proof sewers and separate rainwater systems. It explicitly says inundation in designated brook valleys can be a natural storage function, not automatically a calamity.

The document identifies A58/N395/N269 access and says public transport is often unavailable between cores. It also retains large supraregional events at Beekse Bergen. These are structural planning facts, not incident-time availability.
No standard open-data licence or fixed update cadence is stated on the PDF; cite as public policy evidence and do not bulk-republish it as an open operational layer.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Hilvarenbeek and Waterschap De Dommel
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Local rainwater, storage, high-water and drought evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal project page inspected 2026-09-03; De Dommel event report 2024-07-13 and seasonal-ban notice 2026-03-30
supports: The municipality states that sewers cannot always handle extreme rain. It names wadi locations in Gelderakkers/Loosche Akkers, Vroonacker and Brouwershof, an infiltration sewer in Leeuwerik and five bergbezinkbassins.

Diessens Broek is a water-storage area in the Reusel, Spruitenstroompje and Rosep catchment that fills during high-water peaks. This is named mechanism and intervention evidence, not a live footprint or proof that adjacent areas are dry.

De Dommel's 13 July 2024 report at https://www.dommel.nl/hevige-buien-zorgen-opnieuw-voor-wateroverlast records 10–72 mm rain, high groundwater and actual use of Diessensbroek storage. It is a dated observed event, not a recurrence probability or T+72 forecast.

De Dommel's 30 March 2026 notice at https://www.dommel.nl/geen-oppervlaktewater-onttrekken-in-het-stroomgebied-van-de-beerze-en-reusel makes the Beerze/Reusel seasonal ban annual from 1 April to 1 November; the high rain-dependent system can fall in days. Firefighting remains an exception.

The public pages state no standard machine-data licence, complete sewer/catchment topology, asset telemetry, design-capacity service level or guaranteed refresh cadence. Missing places and operating states remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027
supports: The profile's top priorities include extreme weather, nature fire and digital disruption of vital infrastructure; overstroming ranks in its top-five impact categories. This is regional expert planning judgment, not a municipal probability.

Dry/hot conditions increase nature-fire risk; dry fires can spread quickly and unpredictably, difficult terrain and bluswater constrain response, and recreation or vulnerable people can materially change consequences.
Extreme rain, drought, cold/snow/ice, heat, storm and fog can reduce road/rail access, overload response and cascade through vital infrastructure beyond the initial weather duration.

The Rhine/Meuse scenario is explicitly a major-river hydrograph after multi-day catchment precipitation. It must not stand in for an unselected Reusel, Rosep, Spruitenstroompje, Wilhelminakanaal, regional-storage or sewer mechanism.

Hilvarenbeek is within the Netherlands–Belgium 15 km risk zone. The profile addresses cross-border risk, but the current Dutch NWB municipality graph contains no Belgian gateway; this is an access/model-scope gap, not proof that routes are unavailable.
No standard redistribution licence or fixed refresh cadence is stated; the profile is public preparedness evidence and should be reviewed at the next plan edition.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current nature-fire alert and material Beekse Bergen transient exposure
evidenceSources.edition: Phase-2/high-risk municipal alert published 2026-08-04; Jaarstukken 2024 published 2025
supports: The 4 August 2026 alert reports prolonged dryness and elevated nature-fire risk, rapid/unpredictable spread especially under hard wind, heightened response vigilance and potentially poor mobile reach. It is a time-bounded current alert, not a permanent probability.

The municipality tells people not to await assistance, to escape toward a public road and perpendicular to fire spread, and to help others. Those public first-action semantics conflict with a purely remote-smoke interpretation of all local fire risk.

Municipal Jaarstukken 2024 at https://www.hilvarenbeek.nl/fileadmin/user_upload/Bestanden/PDF-documenten/Jaarstukken_2024.pdf state festival weekends at Beekse Bergen drew approximately 60,000–90,000 visitors and record work on crisis organization and controllable nature fire.

The 2026 Decibel permit and municipal access notice document a multi-day festival/camping period and temporary surrounding-road closures. Event dates, attendance and closures are time-bounded and must not be projected to arbitrary scenarios.

A visitor range does not establish hourly occupancy, mobility, shelter, medical demand or evacuation capacity. The public pages have no standard open-data licence or guaranteed incident-update cadence.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — LIWO 2025.1.6 breach-candidate scope
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; public OGC catalogue inspected 2026-09-03
supports: Exact point-in-polygon containment against the 998-position 2025 non-generalized boundary finds zero primary, two regional and zero regional-water-system or outside-dike catalogue points inside GM0798. The regional points are [5.1785, 51.5052] and [5.1788, 51.5059].

The two points are candidate catalogue entries with generic name/code and frequency flags; they do not select a breach, waterbody, control state, hydrograph, connected footprint, depth, velocity, arrival, duration or recession.

Zero matches in the other three searched candidate layers are scoped no-matches, not evidence that local brook, canal, storage, groundwater, sewer, overland-flow or unregistered mechanisms are absent.

Causal use requires expert selection plus pinned release/layer, source water, defence/breach/control variant, model/scenario dates, native CRS/resolution/units/NoData, uncertainty, scenario-clock mapping and approved licence.
LIWO is release-versioned professional scenario information rather than a live forecast; no blanket standard redistribution licence or fixed cadence was established from the portal.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting and Netbeheer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Water-chain, utility responsibility and capacity-context registers
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot 2026-09-03; Mijn Aansluiting point query 2026-09-03; NBNL sample 2026-09-02
supports: The deployed partial HWH context assigns 85 objects to GM0798: six sewer pumps, RWZI Biest-Houtakker, four surface-water pumps and 74 weirs. Named pumps include Slibbroek, Goirlesedijk, Koppelstraat and Roovert.

HWH is contributor-dependent national register context under CC BY-SA 4.0. Object status, register capacity and timestamps are not live telemetry, connectivity, working capacity, energy dependency, reserve, damage or restoration.

Exact point containment in live public-domain Mijn Aansluiting provider polygons identifies Enexis electricity/gas and Brabant Water drinking water at the municipal center; KPN and DELTA fixed-media polygons overlap. Sewer and heat return no containing polygon and remain Unknown.
The one public NBNL sample for postcode 5081ER returns no-published-match. That is a sample/coverage result, not zero congestion, zero assets, unused capacity or absence of an Enexis service area.

Mijn Aansluiting polygons have provider-specific timestamps but are responsibility context, not cables, feeders, pipes, pressure zones, mobile coverage, live state, backup or restoration. NBNL states at least quarterly capacity/project and monthly queue updates, with no exact licence identifier found.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM, DUO, RDI/Antennebureau, Rijkswaterstaat, KNMI and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public care, education, telecom, water and observation context
supports: No surveyed emergency department lies in GM0798; Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis in Tilburg is nearest at approximately 7.77 km straight-line from the reference point and is listed 24/7. Annual rooms/visits do not establish incident acceptance, staffing, route time or available capacity. RIVM source data are CC0.

DUO registers thirteen current education-use locations, seven primary and six other registered education. Daily CC BY records do not establish occupancy, shelter role, accessibility, supplies, staff or generator endurance.

RDI registers 57 antenna installations: 27 mobile-communication, 22 fixed-link, six amateur, one broadcast and one other-mobile site. The WFS states no fees/access constraints but no reuse licence or cadence; points do not establish coverage, operator, backhaul, backup, congestion, damage or restoration.

Fresh Waterinfo observations at Haghorst Sluis 4 include point levels and discharge around 2026-09-02T17:30Z, while the nearest cached T+72 forecast site is off-municipality. Waterinfo is generally CC0, around ten-minute and non-mission-critical; points do not prove municipal flood safety or control state.

No KNMI station lies inside GM0798; Eindhoven Airport was nearest at about 16.38 km in the deployed 2026-09-02T23:30Z observation. The 48-hour official warning product had no issued warning at its fallback time, which does not establish future or scenario conditions at T+48–72.

One indicative hourly RIVM PM2.5 station lies in Biest-Houtakker and the nearest NDW situation was about 6.88 km from the center. A station is not a smoke plume and no matched road event is not proof that A58/N269/N395/local roads are open.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudburst, flash runoff, fire spread, alerting and event egress; actual controls, roads, hospitals, crews and restoration remain Unknown.

findings.summary: A generic corridor produces unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation in Hilvarenbeek.
findings.evidence: E02/E03 describe Reusel/Rosep/Spruitenstroompje, Wilhelminakanaal, brook-valley storage, groundwater and sewer mechanisms. E06 finds zero primary LIWO candidate but two regional candidates in the full boundary. Canonical river nevertheless holds normalized direct inundation stress 1.497411 at T+24/T+72, with 8,441/8,972 affected and 143,011.575/565,839.403 cumulative person-hours. No selected hydrograph, candidate, waterbody, control/breach state, footprint, depth, arrival, duration or recession supports those consequences.
findings.action: Suppress GM0798's named-major-river local result to Unknown/numerically neutral until a connected major-river scenario exists. Preserve the two regional candidates and all brook/canal/storage/groundwater/sewer mechanisms as unresolved. Add a separate expert-selected regional-water adapter rather than relabeling the generic scalar.

findings.summary: The neighbourhood flood ranking is not driven by the documented local catchment, storage or sewer system.
findings.evidence: At pluvial T+24 the model reports 0.557935 normalized water stress, 3,365 affected and ranks Diessen first, then Verspreide huizen Haghorst, then Hilvarenbeek. E03 supports real water sensitivity and named interventions, but provides no basis for this order. The exact same order appears for storm, river, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire-smoke and compound; no AHN flow path, stress-test cell, Reusel/Rosep/Spruitenstroompje state, Diessens Broek operation, sewer basin or groundwater antecedent is sampled.
findings.action: Mark current local flood ranks unsupported. Obtain the native Hart van Brabant/municipal stress-test surface or a current successor and combine it with AHN, IMWA hydro/controls and licensed sewer context. Retain event, antecedent state, resolution, units, edition, NoData, uncertainty and licence, and test wet-storage versus built-up wateroverlast separately.

findings.summary: The remote-smoke preset omits locally material forest/recreation ignition and first-action behavior.
findings.evidence: E02 maps multiple forest/heath/nature areas, E04 ranks nature fire among likely regional risks, and E05 is a current municipal phase-2/high-risk alert that warns of rapid spread, poor mobile reach and immediate evacuation. Canonical wildfire T+24 has direct flame 0, smoke 0.208545, drought 0.477263 and zero modeled affected people. Its neighbourhood order is the same seed used by water and cyber. This scoped remote-fire result is valid only for its configured distant source; it does not test Hilvarenbeek's local nature-fire risk.
findings.action: Retain zero direct flame for the canonical remote source, but add a clearly separate local-fire scenario with an explicit ignition/perimeter, combustible land cover, fuel/moisture, timestamped wind, access, bluswater/suppression and visitor state. Suppress neighbourhood flame ranks until source-aware allocation is tested.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure can understate Beekse Bergen festival-period demand by several times the municipality population.
findings.evidence: The engine caps affected people against 16,149 residents. E05 says 2024 festival weekends drew approximately 60,000–90,000 visitors and the 2026 Decibel permit included three event days plus camping through Monday. GTFS contains Safaripark/Speelland stops, but no attendance, hourly occupancy, camping population, vehicles, accessibility, care demand or evacuation capacity enters the model. Those historic ranges must not be assumed outside the named event period.
findings.action: Add an optional event-time transient-population overlay with source/event/version, valid-from/to, uncertainty range, venue/camping polygons, arrival/departure profile and double-count controls. Keep baseline occupancy Unknown outside valid windows and test fire, heat, storm, telecom and mobility demand sensitivity without overwriting CBS resident totals.

findings.summary: Four Dutch border links omit core-to-corridor, Belgian-gateway and event-closure constraints.
findings.evidence: E01 supplies A58/N269/N395 edge crossings and no rail station; E02 says public transport is often absent between cores; E04 places Hilvarenbeek in the Belgian risk zone; E05 records time-bounded Beekse Bergen road closures and congestion. Yet the model treats four links as scenario-unit corridors, with the 0.299 km A58 edge able to represent municipality mobility/supply without local approach, Belgian gateway, road closure, bridge/canal crossing, response travel or event egress state.
findings.action: Retain NWB links as Mobility/Supply-only proxies. Add explicit core/venue gateways and scenario-valid NDW/municipal closure inputs; evaluate an authoritative Belgian road gateway under compatible terms. Never infer utility flow, passability or evacuation throughput from an edge crossing.

findings.summary: Public provider and water registers do not calibrate service availability or restoration.
findings.evidence: E07 identifies Enexis, Brabant Water, overlapping KPN/DELTA media territory and 85 partial HWH objects, while the NBNL sample is no-published-match. None supplies feeder/pipe/backhaul connectivity, live load/pressure, switching, pump dependency, backup, priority customers, damage, crews or restoration. Exact compound T+24 values down to six decimals are therefore synthetic. Empty sewer/heat territory and absent capacity sample remain Unknown.
findings.action: Keep all public objects and provider territories affectsSimulation=false. Seek security-reviewed operator exercise zones and aggregate continuity/restoration bands. If unavailable, retain editable service-specific synthetic priors with sensitivity and a prominent non-operational label; do not reuse roads as utilities.

findings.summary: External acute care, registered schools and antenna points are not operational response capacity.
findings.evidence: E08 finds no surveyed ED inside GM0798, the nearest listed 24/7 ED about 7.77 km away, thirteen education locations and 57 antenna installations. E05 warns mobile reach may be poor in nature. These points do not establish ambulance route/acceptance, bed/staff capacity, shelter designation, occupancy, backhaul, signal coverage, power backup or congestion. Facilities 0.511352 and telecom 0.256542 at compound T+24 are not observed states.
findings.action: Expose these registers as dated context. Add external-care routing only with travel and acceptance semantics, shelters only when designated, and communication coverage/backup only with authorized data. Preserve unknown operating state at every checkpoint.

findings.summary: Fresh point observations and a finite warning horizon cannot validate arbitrary 72-hour scenarios.
findings.evidence: E08 contains fresh Waterinfo values at Haghorst Sluis 4, one indicative PM2.5 station, off-site KNMI weather and a 48-hour warning product with no warning at retrieval. None is a municipal gridded forecast or selected scenario footprint; the Waterinfo T+72 location is off-municipality. Projecting a normal point class or no warning through T+72 would conflate observed, forecast, scenario and Unknown states.
findings.action: Keep valid/issue/retrieval time, location, quality, horizon and evidence class visible. Do not interpolate or extrapolate these records into the scenario engine without a documented adapter; after horizon or outside coverage show Unknown, not normal/safe.

findings.summary: Scoped zero results and generic scenarios must not become municipality-wide all-clears.
findings.evidence: Canonical coastal water and earthquake ground motion are exactly zero at T+24, and remote wildfire direct flame is zero. Those are narrow configured-source results: they do not prove no indirect coastal supply/wind consequence, no local or remote seismic event, or no local fire. Conversely, nonzero heat, winter, cyber and storm outputs lack observed/local calibration. The same seed order provides no hazard-specific evidence.
findings.action: Label every preset as a deterministic exercise with named mechanism/source. Retain the narrow coastal and remote-source zeros, but display unresolved local/indirect pathways separately as Unknown. Require source/event/footprint evidence before operational use.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, places, settlements, routes and null semantics are coherent and provenance-bearing.
findings.evidence: E01 resolves GM0798 and its 2025 boundary/statistics, eleven neighbourhoods, five BAG places, twenty-five BRT settlements, four NWB links, zero in-boundary station and thirty scheduled stop areas. The six-person rounded population difference is disclosed. District heating and public charging are null in all rows and are not converted to zero. Roads affect only Mobility/Supply.
findings.action: Retain publisher, edition, retrieval, licence, source membership and null/NoData semantics; refresh at source cadence and rerun focused plus national gates after every snapshot.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic, causal, reconciliation and layer-invariance contract passes.
findings.evidence: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0798 pnpm audit:model passes two tests across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/bounded; zero-intensity semantics are exact; demand/delivery and local population reconcile; route flow is bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; ledgers close; and selected map layers do not alter state.
findings.action: Retain these regression gates while integrating authoritative spatial adapters; never weaken arithmetic or zero/Unknown semantics to conceal calibration gaps.
